newsitem.title: UK: Sterling debt and futures closing report.
newsitem.headline: Sterling debt and futures closing report.

text.p: Gilts rocketed in the European afternoon, gaining almost a point and outperforming across the board as Bunds and U.S. Treasuries struggled to make headway.
The June gilt future was 26/32 up on the session at 110-16 by 1500 GMT. Just two hours previously it had been skulking below 110-00.
"There was talk of a U.S. house being caught short and a big squeeze being put on," said one trader. "But whatever the reason, it's been a hell of a move and very surprising."
The trader said a whole series of stops had been taken out around 110-15, forcing dealers to buy into the market.
The gilt/Bund spread rocketed in to 176 basis points from around 186 late on Thursday -- impressive outperformance in any terms. The June Bund future was up just 19 basis points at 101.15.
David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy, said the writing had been on the wall for a few days, since the gilt/Bund spread reached beyond 190 basis points early this week.
"Everyone's suddenly discovered gilts again. There's a lot of spread trading going on," Coleman said. "We've seen it on several occasions. As soon as we get above 190, buyers come flooding back in."
Coleman said Thursday's election held few fears for the gilt market. A workable majority for Tony Blair's opposition Labour Party is all the market wants now.
"People are now viewing the election in a benign light. They think there will be a fiscal tightening while rates will not head too much higher," Coleman said.
Latest polls put Labour a gaping 18 points ahead of John Major's beleaguered Conservative Party.
"It's a post-election rally starting early," another trader said of the gilt's surge higher.
But any post-election rally on Friday could be choked off quickly with the key U.S. employment report due at 1230 GMT.

Markets across the globe are on tenterhooks because a strong report which may force the Federal Reserve to consider raising interest rates. A Reuter poll forecast a robust 211,000 increase in non-farm payrolls in April.

Some traders suggested that the UK bond future was being whipped around in thin trade. But with nearly 75,000 contracts having changed hands by 1515 GMT, the market has seen many quieter days recently.

With Germany, France, Italy and Spain all on holiday on Thursday, there were fewer investors in the cash market. On top of that, the looming U.S. jobs report was keeping people on the sidelines, dealers said.
"If people want to take any big bets in this environment, the market can move hugely," a gilts salesman said. "But we're switching shorter now anyway."
At the short-end of the market, the June short sterling future settled one basis point higher at 93.39, discounting a half-point interest rate rise within two months.
The June gilt eventually settled 29/32 higher at 110-19.
